thread:
maria: FYI I opened a PR that updates the audit export doc with a short pseudonymization example and tweaks SOC2-friendly wording for EU data residency. link: https://github.com/redwoodinc/docs/pull/432
jon: Thanks — can you call out the concrete TTLs we recommend? Legal usually wants ranges not exact commits.
maria: I added a table draft in the PR description: 30 days (short), 1 year (default), 7 years (archival for legal holds). Open to wording.
samir: Heads-up — in EU wording avoid implying we can delete customer data unilaterally. Suggest: "Retention may be configured per-tenant and amended as required by law or contract." Also request an explicit note on pseudonymization vs anonymization.
arjun: Quick ask: could you include a Go SDK snippet showing export with a pseudonymize hook? I can test locally.
maria: Good call. Posting a compact example here:
```
// Go export example: pseudonymize email and redact ip
client.ExportAuditEvents(ctx, ExportOptions{
  Query: "resource:type=api_call",
  Transformer: func(e Event) Event {
    if e.Fields["email"] != nil {
      e.Fields["email"] = pseudonymize(e.Fields["email"].(string))
    }
    delete(e.Fields, "ip")
    return e
  },
})
```
jon: Nice. Minor nit: rename Transformer -> TransformFunc to match SDK.
arjun: I ran the snippet against local dev export — failing because the example uses delete(e.Fields, "ip") but e.Fields is a typed map[string]interface{}; needs a helper RedactField(e, "ip"). I'll send a small patch.
docs-bot: Linkcheck failed for doc: /security/audit-export.md — missing anchor #pseudonymization-example :link_broken:
maria: thanks bot. I updated heading id in the doc and force-pushed the snippet fix from arjun.
samir: wording LGTM aside from one line: remove wording "we will delete" — replace with "customers can configure deletion or retention according to their contract and applicable law." Also add "when feasible, we pseudonymize personal identifiers prior to export".
jon: Can someone add a one-line migration note for teams shifting from legacy flat JSON to structured events? We should include a curl example and a short SQL sample to map old fields.
maria: added migration note + curl example in PR body. curl example:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/export -d '{"query":"...","format":"jsonl"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' > export.jsonl
jq -r '.fields | @json' export.jsonl | ./map-legacy-to-structured.sh > structured.jsonl
```
arjun: Integration tests flagged a lint error in the fenced code block (missing language tag). I fixed and pushed.
docs-bot: Preview build successful: https://deploy-preview-432--docs.redwood.ai/security/audit-export.html :white_check_mark:
maria: Thanks all. @samir can you add a short approval comment on the PR so eng can merge for the next docs release?
samir: Approved for legal wording. Add a follow-up issue for translation/localization team to review EU phrasing.
jon: Also please add a small note in the console changelog so CS can triage tenant-level retention questions.
maria: Will do. Merging in 10 if no blockers. :rocket:
arjun: No blockers from eng. :+1:
maria: merged and released in docs v1.14.0. Thanks everyone.
